decision: Retain u_injb distributed; do not promote or change protocol
method: Static RTL source and nonblocking edge ordering; no simulator or new synthesis
fact_status: Confirmed source behavior; counterexamples are legal RTL-interface schedules, not executed Pico/UART timing traces
ready_valid_fact: No injection per-byte ready port exists. ia/i_re/iv1/iv2 issue automatically, u_valid can contain gaps, and dq_s_ready is only the packet descriptor/first-byte capacity check.
unchanged_contracts: INJ_DATA/GO register writes and original bus ACK
16bit injection length with no <=2048 or <=written-byte admission restriction
Original single ig_pend and live ilen/its overwrite by busy GO
iwp saturation and restart at final issued read
Byte order and RX descriptor/drop semantics
rejection_of_simple_read_pause: Gating the actual RAM re during effective inj_we and holding its request inserts bubbles. The current read request/ib1/il1 must all stall together; advancing any of them loses/reorders bytes.

Even perfectly aligned stalls change data versions: the original logical same-edge read obtains pre-write data, whereas a delayed physical read obtains the new data. Read-first simulation does not license a prohibited physical collision.
Stalls extend ibusy. A network first byte that arrived after old ibusy cleared may now be dropped; this changes packet arbitration and st_drop, not just latency.
A busy GO changes live ilen/its and future last-byte tests. Moving ioff progress relative to the unchanged GO event can change truncation/extension/descriptor timing.

counterexamples.name: first read of newly overwritten word
counterexamples.preconditions: TX_WAW9, iwp1, an active injection whose length includes word1; first pending read has i_ra1 and prior iq is word0. INJ_GO does not require every requested word already written.
counterexamples.edge0: Effective inj_we writes word1=B while i_re reads word1, whose pre-edge initialized or earlier value is A.
counterexamples.original: RTL read q becomes A; the corresponding byte is emitted from A.
counterexamples.paused_read: RAM read is suppressed; retry after the write obtains B and emits that byte from B.
counterexamples.conclusion: Choosing A!=B changes payload. Existing iq cannot supply A on a first read of this word.

counterexamples.name: length beyond physical buffer wraps into restarted writes
counterexamples.preconditions: Length2049 is accepted unchanged; byte2048 addresses word0 because i_ra uses only ioff[TX_WAW+1:2].
counterexamples.edge0: ia issues final read of word0 and resets iwp0 immediately.
counterexamples.edge1: That registered read samples while a new effective INJ_DATA writes word0; both signals are allowed by source.
counterexamples.conclusion: Same old/new data-version conflict; adding len<=2048 would be a protocol change. This is a source-interface schedule, not a claim a specific serial command delay was measured.

latency_contract_if_pause_were_selected: Each denied read adds at least1 control clock; sustained writes can stall without a finite bound. RX IRQ/descriptor availability and network exclusion window move. GO/ACK events are unchanged, so payload overwrite outcomes can also move. This fails the requested full old contract and is not adopted.
alternatives_not_adopted: A new busy-write/GO restriction or delayed bus ACK changes the protocol/timing contract
A full distributed version mirror defeats the LUT-storage saving
A new faster/phase-shifted memory clock requires a new clock/timing design and is outside this lossless migration
source_contract: The combined source keeps the exact proven TX/console host_mbx body: u_injb has no STAGE2B_BLOCK opt-in; only TXshadow is promoted. No GO, ACK, length, write pointer or stream expression is changed for injection.
physical_pending: Other selected stores still require actual primitive CEB/BLKSEL/OCE/AD review at stage3; this review claims no silicon collision guarantee.
